article_title: UAB/SNMMI Nuclear Medicine Therapy Intensive: Advancing Competence and Innovation in Radiopharmaceutical Therapy.
citation: Glasgow KW, Brady AB. (2025). UAB/SNMMI Nuclear Medicine Therapy Intensive: Advancing Competence and Innovation in Radiopharmaceutical Therapy. Journal of Nuclear Medicine Technology. https://doi.org/10.2967/jnmt.125.271222
title: Weeklong intensive integrating didactic instruction, simulation, interprofessional collaboration, industry engagement, and an innovative capstone across six curricular themes
description: The UAB/SNMMI Nuclear Medicine Therapy Intensive is a weeklong, practice-focused advanced education program for board-certified NMTs and NMAAs that integrates "didactic instruction, simulation-based learning, interprofessional collaboration, and innovative capstone experiences". Its curriculum is organized across "6 major themes": foundations in RPT, radiation safety and compliance, patient-centered communication and eligibility, simulation and applied skills, clinical trials and research literacy, and an escape-room capstone. Program integration and assessment occur through pretests, posttests, team projects, and a challenge activity.
requirements: Qualified, board-certified nuclear medicine professionals already in active practice
Enrollment capped to preserve small-group interaction and personalized mentorship
Access to therapy suites, dosimetry labs, and expert faculty for simulations and tours
constraints: Currently offered only annually in the spring
Applications require a letter of recommendation, statement of purpose, video submission, and documented therapy experience
target_learning_goals: Radiation safety and regulatory compliance in radiopharmaceutical therapy
Patient eligibility assessment and therapeutic communication
Radiopharmaceutical preparation, administration, dosimetry, and follow-up care
Interprofessional collaboration and clinical trial literacy
examples: Curriculum mapped to activities in Table 1, including a therapy simulation lab with mock patient setup, dose calculation, and administration workflow
Industry partners delivered lectures, demonstrations, and hands-on software training throughout the week

The program culminated in a nuclear medicine therapy escape room integrating dose calculation, radiopharmaceutical selection, workflow problem-solving, and safety decision-making in a timed, team-based format

article_title: Performance measures of racially underrepresented Ph.D. students in biomedical sciences: The UAMS IMSD Program Outcomes.
citation: Williams Tremaine B., Prince Latrina Y., Allen Antiño R., Sterba Kristen M., Thomas Billy R., McGehee Robert E. (2021). Performance measures of racially underrepresented Ph.D. students in biomedical sciences: The UAMS IMSD Program Outcomes. PLoS ONE 16(2): e0246683. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0246683
title: UAMS IMSD program: a bundle of curricular and co-curricular support initiatives for UR biomedical Ph.D. trainees
description: The UAMS Initiative for Maximizing Student Development is a NIH-NIGMS funded program to increase the pool of individuals from underrepresented groups earning biomedical science Ph.D.s and transitioning into research careers. Its stated activities are "1) a formal peer mentoring: 2) a five-week summer transition program; 3) competency-based academic portfolio management; 4) a seminar series highlighting minority role models, and 5) active learning-based biochemistry course." Across 10 years (2008–2018), UR trainees made up 21% of biomedical doctoral enrollment on average with a mean GPA of 3.25.
requirements: Trainees are admitted into the program prior to graduate study; the summer transition program is required for all admitted trainees in the summer before their first semester.
constraints: All 37 sampled trainees were exposed to all initiatives of the UAMS IMSD program, so initiative-specific effects could not be separated in this study.
target_learners: Racially underrepresented, first-generation, and disabled doctoral trainees in biomedical sciences
target_learning_goals: Completion of a biomedical science Ph.D. and transition into research workforce careers
examples: The five-week summer program combined about 15 hours weekly of formal lectures in fundamental biomedical research areas, 20 hours weekly of research lab rotations, and 10 hours of psychosocial seminars on cohort building and learning strategies.
